title: Your own work website

hero.alt: Bart's work website: his name, office hours Monday to Friday with a sign-up button, and a projects card
The office-hours sign-up page: open 15-minute times for each day

intro: A work page with an office-hours sign-up, live on the internet. Part 1 builds it on your laptop. Part 2 publishes it.

steps.title: Sign in with your Stanford account
steps.body: Same steps as Setting up Claude.

steps.title: Pick Opus 5.5, Medium
steps.body: The Stanford account doesn't include Fable.

steps.title: Open the Code tab
steps.body: Tell it what you want to do, in your own words, or you can try to sound real nerdy, like Bart:
steps.say: Hi Claude, I want to make a real website with GitHub and Vercel.

steps.title: Answer its first questions
steps.body: What kind of site? Choose Other and type "for work!". How to build it?
steps.say: You decide, I'm not that technical.

steps.title: Pick a folder
steps.body: Where the site lives on your laptop.

steps.title: Say what it's for
steps.body: In your own words: what you're working on, an office-hours sign-up.

steps.title: Allow access
steps.body: Click Allow Once, or a longer option if it offers one.

steps.title: Tell it about your work
steps.body: Answer its questions. Then it builds the page.

parts.label: Part 2
parts.title: Publish it
parts.lede: The accounts are the fiddly part. Have a helper nearby.

steps.title: Ask for office hours
steps.say: Hey, make a nice office hours signup thing for me. Vercel has a thing we can use for that, right? Give me a private page with a passcode where I can set the slots, see who signed up, etc. But also, I want to be able to add those student signups to my calendar. What's the easiest way?

steps.title: Say GitHub is scary
steps.body: When it asks you to sign in to GitHub, where your site's files live.

steps.title: Say no to the shortcut
steps.body: It may offer to skip GitHub. Don't.
steps.say: No, I want to use GitHub, but it's scary. Explain it in one sentence and then make it really easy for me to sign up.

steps.title: Create your GitHub account
steps.body: Claude opens the page for you.
steps.trap: Click SIGN UP, not LOG IN.

steps.title: Connect Claude to GitHub
steps.body: If the instructions mention a terminal, ask. It opens a page and gives you a code to type.
steps.say: That's too complicated for me. Open the page for me and just tell me what to type.

steps.title: Create your Vercel account
steps.body: Sign Up is small, at the bottom. Then Continue with Google.

steps.title: Link Vercel to GitHub
steps.body: Log in to Vercel again and connect it to GitHub.

steps.title: Click Install
steps.body: Vercel asks to install the GitHub connection. Click Install.

steps.title: Connect your repo
steps.body: Pick the one Claude just made.

steps.title: Keep it inside Vercel
steps.body: If it suggests another service (mine said Upstash), say no.
steps.say: No, simpler. Keep everything inside Vercel.

steps.title: Let Claude publish it
steps.body: It gives you your site's address.

steps.title: Add your open times
steps.body: On your private page. Claude gives you the address and passcode.

items.when: Too complicated, or it mentions a terminal
items.say: That's too complicated for me. Open the page for me and just tell me what to type.

items.when: You don't know what something is

items.say: No, simpler. Keep everything inside Vercel.

items.when: It asks you to pick a technical option
items.say: You decide, I'm not that technical.
